newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Glenayre down but call buys seen.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Glenayre down but call buys seen.

text.p: Another company's quarterly earnings fell short of some expectations and investors quickly dumped the stock, but some options investors were picking up out-of-the-money calls hoping for a rebound, traders said Thursday.
This time the victim was Glenayre Technologies Inc, which was down 4-3/8 at 15-1/4 in heavy afternoon trading. More than 7.9 million shares changed hands.
The stock reached a session low of 14-3/4, a level not seen since August 1994.

Late Wednesday, the company, which provides equipment to the wireless telecommunications industry, reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.27 a share, in line with First Call estimates but still short of some expectations.
"The earnings disappointed Wall Street," one options trader said. "It's the same old thing. Disappoint and you get your head handed to you."
He added that the stock had been in a steady downtrend for several months.
As recently as last November, the shares were trading in the mid-20 region.
Among the options, the February 15 call was most active, with volume of more than 1,100 contracts. The February 20 call traded about 215, the March 17-1/2 about 315 and the September 17-1/2 125.
"People are buying the out-of-the-money calls, taking a cheap shot," the trader said.
He added that a couple of sizable buy-writes also crossed, where an investor bought the stock and wrote the calls.
Among Glenayre puts, the most active was the March 17-1/2 with volume of about 315 contracts.
The stock's decline drove options volatilities higher.
In other trading, an investor in Enron Corp options apparently shifted a position.
The Enron February 45 put and the July 45 put each traded 4,000 contracts by afternoon. The stock was up 1/4 at 41-1/3.
"Somebody bought back the Enron February 45 puts and sold the July 45 puts," Harrison Roth, senior options strategist at Cowen & Co said.
In each of those two options, 3,000 of the contracts traded before midday.
Those two Enron puts were the most active puts traded at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
The busiest put overall was the Intel Corp February 155, which traded about 6,415 contracts. With Intel shares extending their recent decline, the option rose 2-7/8 points to six.
Intel shares were down five at 152-1/4. The stock has dropped from 164-3/4, where it closed on Tuesday.
The Intel February 155 call was the busiest option around, with volume of about 12,650 contracts. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
